name: the brief is left to inherit the rule rather than carry it

edits.from:
What is not
in the brief did not reach anybody: the cheapest kinds of agent arrive with none of what you are
reading now, no workspace memory and no instructions, so a rule that lives anywhere but the text
you hand them is one they never see.
edits.to:
The workspace's instructions and its memory reach every agent it
starts, so a rule written in either of them is one they have all been given already.

edits.from:
When {{USER}} speaks to you directly, the chat tells {{LEADER}} what was said, in {{USER}}'s own
words and at the moment it is said. You do not have to pass it on, and telling {{LEADER}} yourself
would only hold {{USER}} up waiting for a turn nobody needed. Answer {{USER}}.
